title: The Hidden Music of Elliptic Curves
subtitle: A guided journey to the Birch and Swinnerton–Dyer conjecture
status: Open Millennium Prize Problem; documentary exposition; no proof claim
claim_boundary: Browser-native, source-normalized exposition of rational points, the Mordell–Weil group, the Hasse–Weil L-function, low-rank theorem terrain, and the strong BSD formula. Numerical agreement, parity, Selmer bounds, family results, one-prime theorems, and p-adic analogues are not promoted to the universal complex conjecture.

plates.label: Cover
plates.title: The Hidden Music of Elliptic Curves
plates.alt: An illuminated cream, navy, and gold cover framing an elliptic curve, arithmetic formulas, and a distant mathematical landscape.

plates.label: Plate I
plates.title: The ancient question of rational solutions
plates.alt: An illustrated map from rational right triangles and cubic curves to sparse rational points, torsion, rank, and the limits of finite search.

plates.label: Plate II
plates.title: Two ledgers in the same hand
plates.alt: A paired arithmetic and analytic panorama links the Mordell–Weil group of rational points to the vanishing of an elliptic-curve L-function.

plates.label: Plate III
plates.title: From prime counts to the central point
plates.alt: Prime-by-prime point counts are assembled into Euler factors and an L-function whose behaviour at the central point is compared with rank.

plates.label: Plate IV
plates.title: The strong BSD ledger
plates.alt: A decorative ledger surrounds the leading-term formula with period, regulator, Tamagawa, torsion, and Tate–Shafarevich contributions.

plates.label: Plate V
plates.title: Islands of theorem, ocean of conjecture
plates.alt: A map distinguishes established modularity and low-rank results from the unresolved higher-rank and universal leading-term frontier.
